summary: logger-libs ships an import-time obfuscated dropper that exec()s a decoded payload with network/subprocess preloaded
details: logger_libs/_compat.py resolves builtins.exec via chr-code concatenation (`getattr(builtins, chr(101)+chr(120)+chr(101)+chr(99))`) and re-exposes it as helper functions named `see_namespace`/`load_module`, concealing the exec reference from literal-token scanners. logger_libs/helper.py reconstructs two base64+XOR-encoded blobs by importing fragments from sibling submodules under logger_libs.themes.theme_NNN and logger_libs.ansi.<name>, decodes them into a URL string and a Python source body, and runs the source through the concealed exec with a namespace preloaded with `requests`, `subprocess`, `sys`, `os`, `wintypes`, `platform`, and the decoded URL. This dropper fires at import time whenever LogHelper is loaded (e.g. `from logger_libs.data_logger.handlers...`), yielding arbitrary code execution on the installer host with network and subprocess primitives in scope. The distribution additionally impersonates adjacent names: setup.py registers `logger_libs` with homepage `https://github.com/wolf1986/logger_libss` (double-s typo) while the README instructs `from logger_util.helper import LogHelper` and references the PyPI package `log-utils`, consistent with typosquat delivery of the dropper under cover of a logging utility.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
